title: Sheinbaum Kicks Off the National Reforestation Day in Puebla; the Goal Is to Plant 6.6 Million Trees in a Day
author: Néstor Jiménez
content:
_This article by Néstor Jiménez originally appeared in the[August 9, 2026
edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/09/politica/sheinbaum-
arranco-en-puebla-la-jornada-nacional-de-reforestacion-el-objetivo-es-
sembrar-66-millones-de-arboles), Mexico's premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**San Nicolás de los Ranchos, Puebla**. From the Iztaccíhuatl-Popocatépetl
National Park, President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo kicked off the National
Reforestation Day, and **decreed that it be repeated every year** , on the
second Sunday of August. And, recalling that this Sunday is also the
International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, she proposed renaming the
Paso de Cortés, which runs between the two volcanoes, and now calling it **"
Paso de los Pueblos Indígenas" (Pass of the Indigenous Peoples)**.

Accompanied by the governor of Puebla, Alejandro Armenta, as well as by the
secretaries of Environment and Natural Resources (Semarnat), of Agriculture
and Rural Development (Sader), of Welfare, of National Defense, and of the
Navy, the president planted a pine and a fir (oyamel). Meanwhile, all the
country's governors, as well as the Head of Government of Mexico City, linked
up through a simultaneous broadcast in each state to also begin the
reforestation day, with the national goal of planting 6.6 million trees on
this day.

![President Claudia Sheinbaum at the launch of the National Reforestation
Day](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reforest-
puebla-02-gal.jpg)President Claudia Sheinbaum began the National Reforestation
Day at the Iztaccihuatl-Popocatepetl National Park, in the Puebla municipality
of San Nicolas de los Ranchos, on August 9, 2026. Photo: Presidencia

With the Popocatépetl in the background, the head of the federal Executive
swore in the environmental defenders. She urged them to "put all your effort,
knowledge, heart, and passion into protecting the natural wealth of Mexico,
made up of forests, jungles, and the other ecosystems of our country; to care
for its natural resources, safeguard its lakes, rivers, mountains, and
mangroves, preserve and strengthen the agricultural zones that sustain us, and
watch over the well-being of the inhabitants of Mexico, of the original
peoples and Afro-Mexican communities."

![President Sheinbaum addresses environmental
defenders](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reforest-
puebla-05-gal.jpg)President Claudia Sheinbaum asked environmental defenders to
put all their effort into protecting Mexico's natural wealth. Photo: Nestor
Jimenez

Recalling that the Sembrando Vida (Sowing Life) program, which began under
former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, already involves 400,000
planters, she added that in eight years they have reforested with **more than
1.5 billion fruit and timber trees**.

She explained that the best-preserved areas of the national territory are
those occupied by the communities, the peoples, the territories of the
Indigenous peoples. "It is there that the conservation of nature has been
demonstrated historically for hundreds of years, for thousands of years. It
was recognized that there could be no development, as we call it today,
without care for the environment and natural resources. Sembrando Vida has
that vision: to recognize the Indigenous peoples, there where the territory
has been preserved and where various schemes have prevented or spread fires or
deforestation, and there to provide sustenance to the communities so they
continue conserving the territory," she added.

For this reason, she proposed changing the name of the Paso de Cortés, since,
moreover, "the peoples passed through here long before. So today, the
International Day of Indigenous Peoples, let us call this pass the Paso de los
Pueblos Indígenas."

![Activists welcome President Sheinbaum at the Izta-Popo
park](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reforest-
puebla-06-gal.jpg)Activists from the Iztaccihuatl-Popocatepetl region welcomed
President Claudia Sheinbaum, who led the work of the National Reforestation
Day. Photo: Presidencia

Mexico is a forest country, in which 70 percent of the territory is covered by
forests, jungles, mangroves, scrublands, and different ecosystems, highlighted
Alicia Bárcena, head of Semarnat. "This restoration is what can undoubtedly
lead us to recover soils, to strengthen the forest economy. The time has come
to make peace with nature, and that is why it is a collective task," said the
federal official.

![Semarnat head Alicia Bárcena at the National Reforestation
Day](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reforest-
puebla-03-gal.jpg)Alicia Barcena, head of Semarnat, took part in the National
Reforestation Day. Photo: Presidencia

Meanwhile, the head of Sader, Columba López, detailed that today more than 6
million trees and more than 1.7 million seeds will be planted directly, while
nearly half a million more will be dispersed with drones in hard-to-reach
areas. In total, **more than 32,000 hectares** will be covered.

![The National Reforestation Day at the Iztaccíhuatl-Popocatépetl National
Park](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/reforest-
puebla-04-gal.jpg)The National Reforestation Day takes place at the
Iztaccihuatl-Popocatepetl National Park, in the municipality of San Nicolas de
los Ranchos, Puebla, on August 9, 2026. Photo: Presidencia

It is "a historic day of reforestation in the Mexican Republic," with an
estimated participation of **more than 241,000 people across the country
reforesting at the same time** , she explained. "From this day on, we commit
to producing and planting 1.5 billion plants and trees, and to also doing so
with seeds, between now and 2030," she added. After calling on the entire
population to join this day, she indicated that on the websites of Sader and
Semarnat there are links to locate the points where these actions will take
place.

She noted that different trees will be planted in each region. For example, in
Aguascalientes, mesquite, palo dulce, and huizache will be planted; in Baja
California, sage and oak; in the southeast, humid-tropic species; and in the
mountainous areas, pines and firs. In addition to mangroves.

As part of the reforestation day, they will use large drones used for the
agricultural sector, which allow seeds to be dispersed in hard-to-reach places
and to cover large areas in a short time. During the event, a demonstration of
seven of these drones was carried out.
